## [3.1.97] - 2026-08-08

### Investigation (no code change): root-caused why home IPv6 sessions still get flagged foreign
`TODO.md` had this flagged as "raised again 2026-08-04, not re-investigated" since the 2026-07-15 session's `/64`-prefix fix apparently didn't fully close it. This session actually root-caused it via `docker logs game_alpha` and `visitors.log` (live evidence, not re-reading old assumptions).

Confirmed: `detectHomeIPv6()` fails on **every** attempt — `⚠️ Could not detect home IPv6 via https://ipv6.icanhazip.com: fetch failed` — because the container runs on the custom `game-net` Docker bridge network (`deploy.sh:43`), which has no outbound IPv6 route by default. `detectedHomeIPv6` never resolves, so `isHomeIP()`'s IPv6 branch always falls through to "foreign" for every IPv6 client, home or not. This is a different bug from the one fixed 2026-07-15 (exact-match vs. `/64`-prefix comparison, which is correct on its own) — the container simply never has an IPv6 address of its own to prefix-compare against. Cross-checked `visitors.log`: the maintainer's own repeated home sessions ("tomasz"/"Tom"/"Tomasz", 2026-07-13 through 08-04) all arrive over real `2600:4041:...` IPv6 addresses — every one of those would have been marked foreign.

Both real fixes carry either infra risk (giving the Docker network real IPv6 routing, untestable headless on a live production box) or an ongoing-maintenance cost (a manual `HOME_IP` override, since the sampled addresses suggest the ISP periodically rotates the delegated prefix) — left as a decision for the maintainer rather than an autonomous change. Full detail and both options: TODO.md "Decisions waiting on the user".

## [3.1.96] - 2026-08-08

### Investigation (no code change): the DOB end-game penalty cannot misfire in the current game
Carried-over concern from the 2026-08-03 CSV-only-reskin audit: `ApprovalService.computeEndGamePenalty` docks every winner -30 days/-$50k unless `dobApprovalStatus === 'approved'`, and `StateService.ts`'s `createNewPlayer` never initializes that field. Flagged as the audit's highest-severity finding and left unverified against the *current, non-reskinned* game — this session closed that gap.

Traced the live CSVs directly: `FINISH` is the only `is_ending_space=Yes` row in `GAME_CONFIG.csv`, and `REG-DOB-FINAL-REVIEW` is the only space whose dice table can output it — no other space, in `MOVEMENT.csv`, `DICE_OUTCOMES.csv`, or `LOGIC_QUESTIONS.csv`, routes to `FINISH`. That space is also the board's only `has_final_review_gate=Yes` row, and the gate is enforced independently in two places — `DiceRollProcessor` discards the roll and force-routes back to the missing examiner, and `MovementService.getValidMoves`/`validateMove` collapse valid moves to the return route — both checking `dobApprovalStatus` live, not a cached flag. Every movement-execution path goes through `movePlayer` → `validateMove`, so there's no route to `FINISH` that skips the check. `tests/ghost/finalReviewStaleIntent.test.ts` already exercises this against the real board topology (via `bootstrapHeadlessServices()`, which loads the actual `public/data/CLEAN_FILES` CSVs), confirming a player missing DOB approval gets routed back to `REG-DOB-PLAN-EXAM` instead of reaching `FINISH`.

The uninitialized field is real but harmless here — it reads as "not approved," which is correct until the player earns it via the DOB exam or Prof-Cert self-certification, and the gate re-checks live state so even a mid-game revoke would correctly re-trigger it. The audit's concern only applies to a hypothetical future reskin CSV that omits a DOB-equivalent gate space entirely — moot for the current board. 68/68 passing across `ApprovalService.test.ts`, `StateService-tryAgainApprovals.test.ts`, `MovementService-unifiedResolver.test.ts`, and `finalReviewStaleIntent.test.ts`.

## [3.1.95] - 2026-08-04

More live-testing feedback on today's board work: bulk-only "restore" buttons and handles that are genuinely hard to tell apart when close together.

### Built: pick which connector to restore, instead of restoring all of them
The "🚫 N hidden · restore" and "↩️ N redirected · restore" pills only ever cleared everything at once — reported as "I need to be able to pick which one gets restored." This was a real gap specifically for hidden connectors (once hidden, an edge has no visible surface left to interact with directly, unlike waypoints/anchors where double-clicking a specific handle already restores just that one).

New shared `RestorablePillDropdown` component: clicking either pill now opens a small list of the affected connectors by readable name (`formatEdgeLabel`, e.g. "Scope Initiation → Fund Initiation"), each with its own restore button, plus "restore all" still available at the bottom for when that's genuinely what's wanted. Replaces both surfaces' previous bulk-only pills — the in-game `BoardToggle` and the standalone Board Layout Editor, which each had their own separate copy of this markup before.

### Fixed: anchor handles were genuinely hard to tell apart from tile dragging
"Grabbing a box and grabbing a node use the same hand icon... so close together." Anchor handles now show a distinct `crosshair` cursor instead of the `grab` cursor shared with tile-dragging and bend-point handles, and hovering an anchor handle immediately highlights its own connector line (thicker, distinct color) — instant confirmation of which line you're about to grab, before pressing down, rather than waiting on the native tooltip's hover delay.

3 new tests (`formatEdgeLabel`) plus a `BoardToggle` test covering the new picker. Full suite: 2646/2646.

## [3.1.94] - 2026-08-04

Two real findings from live-testing v3.1.93: anchor-pinned connectors grabbed "pretty randomly" when several shared a spot, and the Board Layout Editor turned out to have no way to hide a connector at all.

### Fixed: anchor handles landed on the same pixel when several edges pinned to one box side
Reported as "it grabs pretty randomly" — several connectors pinned to the same side of the same hub tile computed to the exact same coordinate (`computeAnchorPoint` only depends on the node's box and the chosen side, so this is deterministic, not a fluke), so their handles stacked exactly on top of each other and a click landed on whichever happened to be on top.

Same fix as the bend-point bundling case shipped earlier today: each colliding handle now spreads to a small deterministic offset (`computeHandleOffset`, already built and tested) instead of stacking invisibly. The new piece is *detecting* the collision in the first place — unlike bend points, two anchors don't need matching coordinates to compare; they only need to reference the same `(node, side)` pair, so `findEdgesAtAnchor` checks that directly against each edge's own source/target node ids rather than resolving or comparing any screen positions. Considered the maintainer's own suggestion (a click-to-open picker menu) but kept the already-shipped offset-handle pattern instead, so the disambiguation gesture stays consistent across bundled bend points and colliding anchors rather than introducing a second, different mechanism for what's the same underlying problem.

5 new tests for `findEdgesAtAnchor`.

### Fixed: the Board Layout Editor had no way to hide a connector
A real pre-existing gap, not something today's other changes broke — `BoardLayoutEditor.tsx` never wired up the per-edge hide feature (`hiddenEdgeIds`/`onHideEdge`) that the in-game admin toggle has had for a while, only the global show/hide-all switch. Wired it in now, reusing the exact same per-device `localStorage` key the in-game toggle already uses — a connector hidden in either tool stays hidden in both, for that admin's own browser. Added the matching "N hidden · restore" pill to the editor's header (mirroring the "N redirected · restore" one from v3.1.90) and a one-line hint that clicking a connector hides it, since the gesture itself isn't otherwise discoverable.

Full suite: 2642/2642.

## [3.1.93] - 2026-08-04

Closes out today's G160 arc: the last of the three original asks (snap a connector's start/end to a fixed spot on its tile box) — the piece flagged as "still ahead" in the last two entries.

### Built: box-side anchor snapping
An admin can now pin either end of a redirected or auto-routed connector to one of a node's 4 side-middle points (top/right/bottom/left) instead of the automatic floating attach point React Flow computes from relative node positions — deliberately just these 4, not free placement along the outline, matching the same "no fuss, discrete choices" philosophy as the bend-point work. Rendered as a small square handle (vs. the round bend-point handles) at each end; dragging always resolves to whichever of the 4 sides is nearest on release — there's no "too far, cancel" case. Double-click releases that end back to the automatic attach point.

Independent of everything shipped earlier today — a connector can have an anchor pin, bend points, both, or neither. Deliberately a **separate** server field (`config.edgeAnchors`, not reshaping the already-deployed `edgeWaypoints` again — see v3.1.92's hotfix for why that's worth avoiding twice in one day) with its own mirrored endpoints (`GET`/`POST /api/instances/:id/edge-anchors`, `DELETE .../edge-anchors/:edgeId/:end`, `DELETE .../edge-anchors`) and client util (`saveEdgeAnchor.ts`). Same permanence model as everything else today: pin it once, every teacher/device/future game sees it.

Implementation stayed contained to the edge component itself — no changes to node components or React Flow `Handle` elements, which would have risked regressing every other edge's default auto-routing. The edge component already reads node positions via `useNodes()` for its own overlap math, so computing "the coordinate of this box's top/right/bottom/left side" is pure geometry (`computeAnchorPoint`/`nearestAnchor` in `boardCommon.ts`), and an anchor override simply substitutes for `sourceX/sourceY`/`targetX/targetY` (and the matching `sourcePosition`/`targetPosition` hint) before handing off to either the bend-point path builder or `SmartEdge`'s own A* auto-routing — so a pinned end can still auto-route through the middle, or be combined with manual bend points, without the two systems needing to know about each other.

2 new pure functions (7 tests), 11 new server unit tests, 4 new endpoint-auth tests, 7 new client util tests. Full suite: 2637/2637. Live-verified the full server round-trip directly (pin both ends → GET reflects both → single-end release preserves the other → invalid anchor name correctly rejected → clear-all). The actual drag-to-a-side gesture in a real browser still needs a live check, same caveat as the rest of today's work.

## [3.1.92] - 2026-08-04

Hotfix for a real crash the maintainer hit immediately after deploying v3.1.91: dragging a redirect handle threw `Uncaught TypeError: i.slice is not a function` and broke the interaction entirely.

### Fixed: v3.1.90's single-point waypoints crashed v3.1.91's array-based code
v3.1.90 shipped storing each edge's redirect as one `{x,y}` object; v3.1.91 (same day) changed the shape to an array of points but never migrated data already saved under the old shape. The one connector the maintainer had redirected between those two versions was still a bare object on disk — `BoardCanvas.tsx`'s new code called `.slice()` on it expecting an array, which a plain object doesn't have.

Fixed at the source: `loadInstance()` in `server/instanceStore.js` now auto-upgrades any old-shape single-point entry into a one-element array the moment it's read, so every caller downstream can assume "always an array" without re-checking. Self-healing — the next save naturally persists the corrected shape, no manual data fix or migration script needed. 2 new tests (upgrades an old entry; leaves an already-correct array alone). Full suite: 2608/2608.

## [3.1.91] - 2026-08-04

Same-day follow-on to v3.1.90's permanent redirect handle: with dragging finally confirmed working live, two real feature requests came out of using it — multiple bend points on longer connectors, and the ability to make several connectors visually merge into one line where they run alongside each other. Researched precedent before building (electrical/schematic "bus" wires — several signals drawn as one thicker line with explicit join/split points — turned out to be the right real-world model; nothing in the React Flow ecosystem does this out of the box, but the interaction pattern the community already uses for draggable multi-point edges, "drag a point on a segment to create a corner," generalized cleanly).

### Changed: one waypoint per edge → an ordered list, scaled by length
`edgeWaypoints[edgeId]` is now `{x,y}[]` everywhere (server config, both API endpoints, the client util, both UI surfaces) instead of a single point. How many points an edge is allowed now scales with its on-screen length — roughly one per 96 flow-units (`maxWaypointsForLength` in `boardCommon.ts`, using flow-space distance rather than the current zoom level so the cap doesn't change as you zoom in and out; 96 is a simple, documented "call it an inch" heuristic since the board has no real physical scale). Dragging any point on an existing segment inserts a new corner there, up to that cap; double-clicking an existing point removes just that one (removing the last one reverts the edge to normal auto-routing, as before).

### Built: manual connector bundling
While dragging a point, if it lands near another edge's point it snaps onto that exact coordinate (`findSnapTarget`, ~12 flow-units). When two or more edges share a run of identical points, that shared stretch renders as one thicker overlay line instead of separately-drawn overlapping ones (`computeSegmentMerges`) — deliberately only the *interior* segments participate (never the ends touching each node, which depend on each edge's own auto-computed attach point) — which conveniently produces exactly the "short individual stub into a shared trunk" look real bus diagrams use, for free.

**How you tell 5 bundled connectors apart to unsnap just one:** each edge's own drag handle spreads to a tiny deterministic offset around the shared point (`computeHandleOffset` — a small fixed "rosette" arrangement, alphabetical by edge id so it's stable across reloads) instead of stacking invisibly on top of its siblings. Every one stays independently visible and grabbable, with a hover tooltip naming which connector it is; the merged *line* itself still draws through the true shared coordinate, so it still reads as one thick line. Dragging one handle away from the shared spot un-merges just that connector — nothing else to clean up, since there's no separate "these are bundled" record to begin with; it's purely geometric.

5 new pure functions in `boardCommon.ts` (`maxWaypointsForLength`, `computeSegmentMerges`, `findSnapTarget`, `computeHandleOffset`, `findEdgesAtPoint`), each independently unit-tested (23 new tests) before wiring into `BoardCanvas.tsx`'s edge component — every piece of the geometry was verified in isolation ahead of the trickier rendering integration. Server/client renamed to match the array shape (`setEdgeWaypoints`, `saveEdgeWaypoints`) with tests updated to match. Full suite: 2606/2606. Live-verified the multi-point server round-trip directly (3-point array POST → GET reflects it → empty array correctly rejected) — the actual drag/snap/bundle gestures in a real browser still need a live check, same caveat as v3.1.90.

### Still ahead
Snapping a connector's start/end to a fixed spot on its tile (4 side-middles, not just the automatic floating attach point) — independent of everything above, not yet built.

## [3.1.90] - 2026-08-04

A same-day follow-on to v3.1.89's G160 session: the maintainer tried the redirect handle live and it silently did nothing (hover cursor worked, drag didn't). A multi-round diagnostic — a red herring CSS fix, console logging that got lost to DevTools scroll/collapse, then an on-screen debug badge — eventually surfaced the real cause: the maintainer had been testing through the **Board Layout Editor**, a separate standalone admin tool that was never wired up to G160 at all. That in turn raised a real design question (should any admin control be reachable mid-game?), which led to keeping the in-game teacher/admin toggle as-is but making G160's redirects work properly in both places, permanently.

### Fixed: G160 redirect handle wasn't reachable from the Board Layout Editor
`BoardLayoutEditor.tsx` mounts `BoardCanvas` with `isAdmin={true}` but never passed `edgeWaypoints`/`onSetEdgeWaypoint`/`onClearEdgeWaypoint` — so the handle rendered (admin mode gates on `isAdmin` alone) but every drag attempt silently no-op'd, since the callback it needed was never there. Confirmed via a live diagnostic round-trip (temporary logging, since removed) that `isAdmin:true` reached the handle correctly while the setter callback read `false` at the exact same point — the tell that this was a wiring gap in one specific caller, not a bug in `BoardCanvas` itself.

### Changed: edge-waypoint redirects are now permanent, not per-device
Previously (v3.1.89) a redirect was pure client-side localStorage — a personal display tweak, invisible to other teachers/devices. Reframed after confirming tile-position drags already persist for real (`/api/instances/:id/positions`, shared classroom config) — a redirect drawn in either the in-game admin toggle or the Board Layout Editor should follow the same rule: fix it once, everyone sees the fix, forever.

New server-side tier mirroring the existing positions endpoint exactly: `config.edgeWaypoints` in the classroom's instance config (`server/instanceStore.js` — `setEdgeWaypoint`/`clearEdgeWaypoint`/`clearAllEdgeWaypoints`, with the same backward-compatible defaulting `insertions` got in Phase 4a), and four new endpoints in `server/server.js` (`GET`/`POST /api/instances/:id/edge-waypoints`, `DELETE .../edge-waypoints/:edgeId`, `DELETE .../edge-waypoints`). Reads are public (pure display data, no gameplay logic involved); writes require the same instance write-token/admin-password/teacher-session check every other classroom mutation uses. Deliberately skipped the CSV-baking pipeline entirely — unlike tile positions, waypoints aren't consumed by the game engine, so there's no resolved-CSV artifact to regenerate; `ensureFreshBake` still runs after each write purely to keep the bake stamp's `configVersion` in sync.

New client util `src/utils/saveEdgeWaypoint.ts` mirrors `saveBoardPosition.ts`'s auth/error contract exactly. `GameLayout.tsx`'s in-game admin toggle and `BoardLayoutEditor.tsx` both now fetch on mount and write through this same util — the old localStorage tier in `GameLayout.tsx` is gone. `BoardLayoutEditor.tsx` also gained a "N redirected · restore all" pill in its header, matching the one the in-game `BoardToggle` already had.

### Decided: in-game admin/teacher board controls stay
Raised and settled a real scope question along the way: should *any* admin control be reachable during a live game? Tile-position dragging already writes permanently (not ephemeral, contrary to an earlier assumption corrected this session), so the concern was legitimate. Decided to keep both the "Edit on/off" toggle (admin-only) and "Edges on/off" declutter control (admin or a logged-in teacher, per its own 2026-07-26 design note) as-is — they're deliberate, gated capabilities for the person actually running a classroom session, not an accidental surface.

Server: 7 new instanceStore unit tests, 4 new endpoint-auth wiring tests. Client: 11 new tests for the new util. Full suite: 2585/2585 passing. Live-verified the full server round-trip against a local instance (POST → GET reflects it → survives a fresh `loadInstance` read from disk → single-edge and clear-all DELETE both work, bake stamp version stays in sync) — the embedded browser tooling used for earlier diagnostics couldn't render board connector lines at all (a known session-level limitation, not a code issue), so the actual drag gesture in a real browser still needs a live check before considering the Board Layout Editor path fully confirmed end-to-end.

## [3.1.89] - 2026-08-02

A short, high-signal follow-on session to v3.1.88: closed the last open naming decision, then built both top-3 handoff items end to end — G160 (per-edge board-connector redirect) and in-game engagement tracking. Naming and engagement tracking were both live-verified (the latter smoke-tested end-to-end against a running server); G160's drag interaction is code-complete and test-covered but couldn't be visually confirmed this session due to a tool limitation in the embedded browser pane (see its entry below) — flagged in TODO.md for a real-device check.

### Decided + built: Bank/Investor/Lender character naming
Closed the last open "Decisions waiting on the user" item. The 6 funding-phase spaces (`BANK-FUND-REVIEW`, `LEND-SCOPE-CHECK`, `INVESTOR-FUND-REVIEW`, each with a first-visit and subsequent-visit variant) had no `CHARACTER_MAP` entry, so their board tiles fell back to the bare phase label ("Funding") instead of a distinguishing discipline badge — same problem DOB/FDNY had before their split (v3.1.x). Named from the existing narration voice already in `Spaces.csv` (Lender: personal/blunt, "pound of flesh"; Bank: institutional, "Underwriting... Standard process"; Investor: committee-driven, "we move real money"). User picked the simple pattern matching Owner/Architect/Engineer/Contractor: **The Bank**, **The Lender**, **The Investor**. Added to `CHARACTER_MAP` in [characters.ts](src/constants/characters.ts) with 3 new colors (teal `#009688`, amber `#FFC107`, indigo `#3F51B5`) chosen distinct from all 6 existing character colors and from each other, since all three share FUNDING's phase color. No portrait art exists for these roles yet — `imageRoles: []`, which falls back to the emoji everywhere a portrait would otherwise show. Updated `tests/services/characters.test.ts`'s stale "every character has portrait art" assumption to explicitly allow the emoji-only opt-out (20/20 passing).

### Built: G160 — per-edge waypoint redirect
The other half of fb:feedback-1778327469678-d27a73d0 ("I would want more control of which lines I want shown **and how they run**") — show/hide shipped v3.1.49; this closes "how they run." An edge that must stay visible but whose A*-auto-routed path (`SmartBezierEdgeTuned`) detours somewhere confusing can now be reshaped by an admin: a small drag handle sits at the midpoint of every edge in board-edit mode (hollow + dashed = not yet redirected, solid + filled = redirected), dragging it drops a single waypoint the edge then routes through as two straight segments — bypassing A* for that edge entirely, so the admin's placement is authoritative rather than a routing hint. Double-clicking a solid handle resets that edge back to normal auto-routing. Deliberately one waypoint per edge, not full spline editing — covers "the detour looks wrong," not general path authoring.

Same per-device localStorage tier as the existing hidden-edges set (`unravel:boardEdgeWaypoints`, keyed by edge id) — a redirect is a display fix for a badly-drawn connector, not real game data, so it doesn't touch CSV/server persistence. `BoardToggle` gets an independent "↩️ N redirected · restore" pill next to the existing "🚫 N hidden · restore" one — kept separate rather than one combined reset, so clearing redirects doesn't discard curated hides or vice versa. The waypoint path math (`buildWaypointEdgePath`) is pulled into `boardCommon.ts` alongside the board's other pure, unit-tested geometry helpers (`computeVisibleEdgeIds`, `resolveTileOverlap`) — 3 new tests.

**Not yet live-verified in a real browser** — see TODO.md's G160 entry. This session's embedded Browser pane wasn't displaying/compositing frames (a documented tool limitation, not a code issue: confirmed via a clean git-revert A/B test that even the unmodified baseline board renders zero edges in that same pane, since the A* smart-edge library needs real layout measurements it never gets without compositing). Typecheck, lint, full build, and the full test suite (2552/2552) are all clean; the drag interaction itself needs one real playthrough before considering this fully done.

### Built: in-game engagement tracking
"How far players get, what draws their attention" — decided earlier this session as a better-scoped replacement for a feedback-triage cadence (the bug-report dashboard already covers that). Reuses the existing acquisition-funnel infrastructure (`PLAYTEST_EVENTS`/`logVisitor`/`POST /api/playtest/track` in `server/server.js`) rather than building anything parallel — three new event names (`space_reached`, `game_finished`, `panel_opened`), all pseudonymous (`gameId`/`playerId` only, never the player's display name).

**Re-scoped one piece of the original spec after thinking through the failure mode:** the spec listed `game_abandoned` as a 4th tracked event, but a reliable "player closed the tab" signal doesn't really exist client-side — `beforeunload`/`visibilitychange` beacons are well known to get silently dropped when a tab is just killed. Instead, abandonment is now *inferred* at aggregation time: any `GAME_STARTED` entry (already logged for every game, no new event needed) whose `gameId` never shows up in a `game_finished` event, more than 4 hours after it started, counts as abandoned. Same actionable answer ("what fraction of started games don't finish"), no flaky new client hook.

**Multi-device double-counting, handled at aggregation, not at the write side:** a shared-screen TV plus several phones (Phones+TV mode) can each independently observe and report the same real moment — e.g. every connected device seeing the same player's space change at once. Rather than building live cross-device dedup (a real project on its own), `space_reached` and `game_finished` are deduped when the stats are computed: unique `(gameId, playerId, spaceId)` triples for space-reach, unique `gameId` for finish. `panel_opened` is NOT deduped — each open is a genuine single local UI click (no cross-device duplication possible), and repeat opens are themselves the signal worth counting.

New pure aggregation module `server/engagementStats.js` (`aggregateEngagementStats`), sibling to the existing `visitorStats.js` but scoped to progression questions instead of acquisition-funnel ones — 11 new unit tests. New admin-gated `GET /api/admin/engagement-stats` endpoint alongside `/api/admin/playtest-stats`. Wired to fire from: `GameLayout.tsx` (space-reached, watching each player's `currentSpace`, deduped per-client via a ref so a busy game doesn't re-fire on every unrelated re-render), `EndGameModal.tsx` (game-finished, once per mount the first time the game reaches any end state — win or loss both count as "finished," distinct from the abandoned inference), and the Rules/Log/Glossary toggles in `GameLayout.tsx` plus the "What to do & why" toggle in `PlayerPanelV2.tsx` (panel-opened). Smoke-tested end-to-end against a local server: posted all 3 events, confirmed the aggregation endpoint reflects them correctly, confirmed the endpoint 401s without admin auth. Typecheck, lint, full build, and the full test suite (2563/2563) all clean.

## [3.1.88] - 2026-08-02

A backlog-clearing session through TODO.md's "Architecture / code health" bucket, dependency-ordered rather than list-order. Most of the "1-2 session, do NOT do casually" items turned out already resolved by past sessions that never removed the TODO line — but three real, previously-unknown bugs surfaced during the verification passes and got fixed. Deployed and bundle-verified live mid-session at commit `8afb6de` (`/health` reporting the exact commit hash, confirming that fix itself works in production for the first time since it shipped in v3.1.87).

### Fixed: `CardService.discardCards` silently dropped its audit-trail arguments
Four call sites passed real `source`/`reason` values (`'manual_effect'`, `'Manual action: Replace W card…'`, plus dice/card-effect reasons from `EffectFactory.ts`/`CardService.ts`'s own `CARD_DISCARD` generators) but the `card_discarded` event only ever emitted a generic "Discarded N cards." Wired `reason` into the log message (`source` rides the event for filtering, matching `card_drawn`'s existing pattern). Checked all `CARD_DISCARD`-effect generators first: every one already sets a specific `reason`, so `CardEffectHandler`'s "Effect processing" fallback text turned out dead-in-practice, not a real gap — a clean fix, not a mixed bag. Live-verified: the game log now reads "Manual action: Replace W card - removing old card" instead of "Discarded 1 card."

### Housekeeping: deleted `EffectFactory.validateCard`, a dead type guard
Zero production callers, and unlike `validatePlayerAction` (deleted last session), no live duplicate to wire it to — every `Card` in this app flows through `DataService`'s typed CSV pipeline, never through an "unknown" boundary this guard was built to defend. Removed the method and its one dedicated test.

### Fixed: `ActiveEffect.effectData: any` — typed the seam CSV-column drift already broke once
The item's own framing ("needs a discriminated union over effect kinds across the whole engine") described work that was already done: the 15-variant `Effect` union + type guards already existed in full in `EffectTypes.ts`. `ActiveEffect.effectData` just wasn't pointed at it. Fixed (`any` → `Effect`); the one real consumer (`EffectEngineService.applyActiveEffects`) now narrows via the existing `isResourceChangeEffect` guard instead of an `as any` cast. Verified the typing was real, not silently `any`, via a throwaway `@ts-expect-error` probe on a bogus field before removing it.

### Fixed: `StateService` double-notifying on 4 of `updateActionCounts`'s 11 call sites
`setAwaitingChoice`, `clearAwaitingChoice`, `setPlayerMoveIntent`, and `clearTurnActions` each called `notifyListeners()` again after `updateActionCounts()`'s own unconditional notify — two listener sweeps per state change instead of one. The other 7 call sites already relied solely on the internal notify, matching its own doc comment. Removed the 4 redundant calls. Ghost-bot gate re-run given this touches every-turn state-notification wiring: 33/33 clean.

### Fixed: `DataService`'s hot-path lookups converted from linear scans to keyed Maps
`getCardById`/`getGameConfigBySpace`/`getMovement` now read from `Map`s built once at load instead of `.find()`ing an array each call — the "134 call sites" the TODO item warned about were all callers of the stable public API, none of which needed to change; the scan lived in one line inside each method. **Found a real bug while verifying, not just a style nit:** ~16 E2E test files use a `NodeDataService`-style helper that populates the backing arrays directly and calls `buildSpaces()` without going through the normal load methods — the first cut of this change (rebuilding the Maps only inside the 3 load methods) left the Maps empty on that path, breaking 23 tests across 8 files. Fixed by centralizing into one `rebuildLookupMaps()` called from both the load methods and `buildSpaces()` itself. Deliberately did NOT extend this to the rest of the file's other `.find()`/`.filter()` calls — a 2026-07-28 benchmark already found zero measurable payoff there. Ghost-bot gate re-run: 33/33 clean.

### Fixed: `getGameState()`/`getPlayer()`/`getAllPlayers()` now do a genuine deep copy
Previously shallow below the top 2 levels — a nested field (`activeCards`/`activeEffects`/`loans`/`moneySources`/etc.) obtained from a "copy" was actually a live reference into real game state. Audited first: grepped `services/` and `components/` for any in-place mutation of these fields — found none anywhere, so the risk was real-in-principle but never yet triggered. Switched to `structuredClone()`. **Found a real performance trap along the way:** a full clone including `globalActionLog` benchmarked at ~5.3ms/call on a realistic late-game state (900 log entries) — 3,400x slower than the old shallow copy, which would have made longer games feel laggy. Fixed by excluding just the log from the clone and handing it out as a plain array copy instead — safe because log entries are permanent/append-only (confirmed via the same grep: nothing anywhere edits an existing entry after it's written). Brings a real call to ~530 microseconds. Live-verified in the browser: a snapshot's nested fields can no longer leak mutations into live state (confirmed via direct injection test). Ghost-bot gate (all 4 variants): 33/33 clean.

### Re-audited and closed: DEF-9 (stale console-call count) and DEF-11 (skipped E2E + process.exit)
DEF-9's tracked "166 raw console.* calls bypass the debug gate" was ~2 months stale: only 12 remain, and 8 of those are legitimate (the debug gate's own implementation, a separate genuinely-used debug-panel toggle system, or deliberate production diagnostics that should stay visible regardless of debug mode). The proposed fix (make `money` a computed getter over `moneySources`) turned out to be based on a wrong premise: `moneySources` only tracks money *received*, by category, never decremented on spend — it exists for an end-game funding summary, not a live decomposition of the current balance. Implementing the proposal as written would have been a real bug (player money would only ever increase). Also structurally infeasible given `Player` is treated as plain JSON-serializable data throughout (WebSocket sync, `structuredClone`, constant spreads) — a computed getter doesn't survive any of that. **While checking whether `moneySources` minus `expenditures` could reconstruct `money` instead, found a real bug:** `FinancialEffectHandler.applyFeeDeduction` (every `FEE_DEDUCTION` effect — regulatory review fees, bank loan fees) correctly deducted cash but never recorded it into `expenditures.fees` — the field whose own type comment documents exactly that job ("All regulatory, consultant, and expeditor costs"). Both the overlay and modal container showed the correct exit-variant styles (`opacity: 0`, the matching transform) with zero console errors — `onClose` fires and React state updates correctly every time. The DOM node just never unmounts, because `AnimatePresence` waits for an exit-animation completion signal that depends on real browser compositing, which this tool's Browser pane doesn't produce unless actually displayed. Escape and backdrop-click share the identical `onClose()` path in `ModalBase`, so there was no need to test each separately once one was root-caused this precisely. ## [3.1.84] - 2026-07-31

### Added: Homeowner Violation mechanic — "Notice of Violation" (L050) and "Immediately Hazardous Violation" (L051)
TODO.md's homeowner-violation-mechanic entry (open since the 2026-07-12 player comment, spec sketched 2026-07-25, fully locked earlier today via maintainer Q&A) is built and shipped. Two new life-event cards, very rare (2 of 51 L cards): drawing either one gives the player a corrective Work Package and starts a 180-day countdown to file an Affidavit of Correction.

**The design, in full.** The civil penalty is sized to the added work, not a flat number: 4%/8% (small tier) or 10%/20% (large tier) of the corrective Work Package's cost, where the rate depends on whether the Affidavit is filed on time (half rate) or late (full rate) — mirroring how real NYC DOB civil penalties scale with corrective-work cost and file-promptly-vs-not. Tier is decided by the player's total project scope at trigger time, split at $500k (proxy for NYC's real 1-2-family-vs-3+-family split, which this game doesn't model directly). L050 is the flat case: file whenever, pay the on-time/late rate, done. L051 ("Immediately Hazardous," matching real DOB's Class 1 violation category) adds a daily penalty — $500/day (small) or $2,000/day (large) — that starts accruing once the 180-day deadline passes unfiled, on top of the eventual filing fee. An unresolved violation at game end is charged the late rate as a backstop.

**New engine ground, not a reskin of an existing card.** No card in the game previously combined "draws more work" with "charges a penalty," and the game had no "keep charging until the player does X" mechanism — only fixed-turn-count recurring effects. L050/L051 are special-cased in `CardService.applyCardEffects` (same pattern as E075 "Backchannel Favor"), bypassing the generic CSV-effect pipeline: `handleNoticeOfViolation` draws the Work Package and sets six new `Player` fields (`violationStatus`/`violationVariant`/`violationTier`/`violationDeadlineDay`/`violationPenaltyBase`/`violationAccrualCheckpoint`), `fileAffidavitOfCorrection()` is the player-initiated action that resolves it, and `processViolationDailyAccrual()` — called once per turn-end via `TurnTransitionHandler` — handles L051's open-ended accrual with a checkpoint so overdue days are never double-charged. Pure fee/tier math lives in `src/utils/violationRules.ts`, kept separate from the stateful side so it's directly unit-testable. `PlayerPanelV2` gets a new status dot + deadline countdown (styled like the existing DOB/FDNY indicators) and a "File Affidavit of Correction" button (`ActionButton`'s first real usage — it existed unwired since an earlier session). `EndGameModal` gets its own warning section for an unresolved violation at game end, independent of and able to render alongside the existing missing-DOB-approval section.

**The six-field `Player` addition needed five sites, not one** — `DataTypes.Player`, `StateTypes.MutablePlayerState`, `StateTypes.PlayerUpdateData`, and both of `TurnStateManager`'s field-by-field copy functions (`extractMutableState`/`cloneMutableState`) — the same shape the DOB/FDNY approval fields already required, and just as easy to silently miss one of.

**Verification.** Typecheck clean throughout, lint unchanged (0 errors / 35 warnings). 15 new `CardService` tests (trigger for both cards, tier boundary at exactly $500k, on-time/late fee math, daily-accrual math including the no-double-charge case) plus a dedicated `violationRules.test.ts`. Live-verified against the actual running app, not just mocks: reached into the live React app's real service instances from the browser console and called the production `CardService` methods directly on a real player — confirmed the corrective Work Package draw, tier classification, the new indicator, an on-time filing charging the correct $14,000 half-rate fee on a $350k Work Package, and the daily-accrual math after forcing simulated time 10 days past the deadline (charged the correct large-tier $20,000). Zero console errors throughout. Full suite: 2582 passed / 1 skipped (183 files), including the 50-game ghost-bot runs, which exercise the two new cards under real random play without incident.

**Two gaps caught in review and closed same day, before this shipped.** (1) The end-game violation backstop wasn't surfaced in `EndGameModal`'s summary screen the way the existing DOB penalty is — added a new `gameState.endGameViolationPenalty` field and its own warning box, live-verified by simulating an unresolved-violation win. (2) `TurnTransitionHandler` — which now runs the daily-accrual check every turn-end — had no dedicated test file at all; added one (13 tests covering its full step sequence, not just the new call). Writing that test also surfaced that the pre-existing end-game win-check branch (home of both the DOB and violation penalties) had zero direct unit coverage before today; added 3 tests there too.

## [3.1.83] - 2026-07-31

### Added: player-to-player trading is reachable and actually works — "Backchannel Favor" (E075)
TODO.md's Parking lot tracked `NegotiationModal`/`NegotiationService` as "fully BUILT but has no trigger" since 2026-07-29. Closer reading found that wasn't the real state of things — the receiving half never worked even when opened, not just unreachable. Fixed both.

**What was actually broken, found while wiring the trigger:** `NegotiationModal`'s negotiation state was local `useState`, never synced from `stateService` — the "Incoming offer — Accept/Decline" screen was real, built UI, but no code path ever showed it to the partner, on any device. `NegotiationService.makeOffer`'s type signature didn't accept money at all — the offer-builder UI collected a dollar amount and `NegotiationModal.handleMakeOffer` silently dropped it before it ever reached the service. Accepting an offer never delivered the cards to the receiving player. Declining lost the offered cards for good — removed from the offerer at offer-time, never returned.

**The fix reuses proven infrastructure instead of patching each bug individually.** `ChoiceService`/`ChoiceModal` already has a shipped, correct mechanism (v3.0.17) for asking a *specific* player — not necessarily the current-turn player — a question that shows up on the right device (per-phone: only their device; shared-screen: the one shared view; already used by `EffectEngineService`'s `PLAYER_AGREEMENT_REQUIRED` and E009's own opponent picker). The partner's accept/decline now goes through that same pipeline instead of a bespoke sync `NegotiationModal` never actually had. `NegotiationService.makeOffer` records the offer, calls `choiceService.createChoice` on the partner, awaits the real response, then resolves the trade inline: money moves via `ResourceService` (skips the transfer, but still delivers the cards, if the initiator can no longer afford it by response time), cards move to the partner on accept or return to the initiator on decline. Scoped to **accept/decline only** for this pass — no counter-offers.

**New card:** E075 "Backchannel Favor" (`E` type, `phase_restriction = Any`) — picks a partner (auto-selected with one opponent, `ChoiceService`-prompted with more, mirroring E009's `handleFavorCalledIn`), then emits a new `negotiation_requested` `GameEvent` that `GameLayout` uses to open `NegotiationModal` pre-seeded with that partner (`initialPartnerId` prop, skips straight to the offer-builder screen). Deleted `NegotiationModal`'s dead `reviewing_offer` render branch in the same pass — confirmed-unreachable code found while fixing this exact file.

**Verification.** Typecheck and lint clean (lint warnings actually dropped, 37→35, from tightening `NegotiationState`'s `context: any`/`offerData: any` into real types). Full suite green. Live-verified with two genuinely separate browser tabs standing in for two phones: Alice played the card, picked Bob, offered $100 → Bob's own tab showed the real offer live over WebSocket with no reload → Accept moved exactly $100 from Alice to Bob. Repeated offering a card instead and hitting Decline: the card returned to Alice, no money moved. Zero console errors from the feature itself throughout (one known, pre-existing, unrelated quirk: `AnimatePresence`-based modals — same as the already-documented `DiceResultModal` issue — sometimes don't visually dismiss in this non-compositing test browser even though the underlying state is already correct; confirmed via the live game-state API each time, not just the screen).

## [3.1.80] - 2026-07-31

### `set-state-in-effect`: 34 → 18, with real research behind the fix rather than a mechanical sweep
The 2026-07-29 audit (`eslint.config.js`) left this permanently `warn` and scoped a real fix as "its own project, or accept it permanently." Researched the rule properly first — React's own docs page for it, the `useSyncExternalStore` migration path, and a live GitHub issue (facebook/react#34743) where other real projects hit the same false-positive shapes this codebase was seeing — before touching any code, so the fix follows React's own paved path rather than a guess.

**Read all 34 flagged sites individually before bucketing them** (the original 9/3/22 estimate from the 2026-07-29 audit undersold the real split once each site was actually read):

- **7 were "subscribe to a store, seed the initial value synchronously"** — `GameLog`, `SpaceExplorerPanel`, `GameLayout` (the big one), `TVDisplay`, `ChoiceModal`, `NegotiationModal`, `PlayerSetup`. All moved to a new [useSyncedGameState](src/hooks/useSyncedGameState.ts) hook wrapping `StateService` in `useSyncExternalStore` — React's own tool for exactly this, and it also sidesteps "tearing" (different components seeing different snapshots mid-render) a manual subscribe+setState can produce. One real wrinkle worth recording: `StateService.getGameState()` deep-copies on every call, so it does **not** return a referentially-stable snapshot between reads — calling it twice with nothing changed yields two different object references, which is exactly what `useSyncExternalStore` requires *not* to happen (React logs "the result of getSnapshot should be cached" and can loop otherwise). Rather than change `getGameState()`'s public contract, the hook caches the snapshot itself and only invalidates it when `StateService`'s own subscribe callback actually fires.
- **7 were "local state that's just a copy of a prop or other state"** — `DiceRollEditor`, `PlayerPanelV2`, `DictionaryPanel` (two sites), and three more in `SpaceExplorerPanel`. Fixed with React's documented "adjusting state when a prop changes" render-time-comparison pattern where the state has other legitimate update paths too (a click can still diverge it from the prop), or a plain `useMemo`/lazy `useState` initializer where it's purely one-time derived data (`DictionaryHint`, `PlaytesterLandingPage`).
- **`GameLayout`'s biggest single site** bundled real logic — clearing per-turn notification state (button feedback, player notifications, approval-revoke banners) on an actual player/turn transition — inside the same subscribe callback that was also duplicating raw state. `useSyncExternalStore` gives no callback to hang that comparison off of, so it's now a small `useRef`-based transition detector, a standard pattern, not a novel one. This was the highest-risk single change in the batch (player-visible notification state, zero prior test coverage) — a new dedicated test file, [GameLayoutTransitionClear.test.tsx](tests/components/layout/GameLayoutTransitionClear.test.tsx) (5 tests), pins: no clear on mount, clears on player change, clears on turn change, does **not** clear on an unrelated field change, clears on unmount.

**The remaining 18 were audited individually, not left by default** — each one either isn't the "state mirrors a prop" shape the fix applies to, or the flag is a static-analysis blind spot rather than a real issue:

- **`BoardCanvas`** (1) — deliberately untouched. This is the exact effect that fixed two real shipped bugs (funding-token `{fundingAmount}` resolve, and First/Subsequent visit-copy staleness — both documented inline in the file). `nodes` mixes ReactFlow-owned state (drag positions from admin edit mode) with derived display data in one array; "just compute it at render time" doesn't apply when the target isn't a pure copy of its inputs. Fixing it properly means separating structural node state from derived display data — a real architecture change, not a pattern swap, and not something to bundle in with 33 unrelated sites.
- **`GameLayout`** (4 remaining) / **`TVDisplay`** / **`useModalQueue`** / **`NegotiationModal`** / **`DictionaryPanel`**'s third site (7 total) — genuine effects: a dice-result tab broadcast keyed on `Date.now()` (needs a fresh id per qualifying result, not expressible as a pure render-time value), two modal-sequencing orchestrators, a one-shot external-request handler, a timed "flash then auto-dismiss" turn-pill indicator, a queue-flush ("open the next payload once idle"), a "start this negotiation" trigger, and an "arm a fallback timer" pattern. None of these are state mirroring a prop; all genuinely need an effect.
- **8 mount-time data-loading sites** (`StatsDashboard`, `ClassroomAdminPanel`, `ClassroomSetup`, `TeacherClassroomPanel`, `ConnectionStatus`, `BugReportsPanel`, `useDictionary`, `AdminGameManager`) — checked each function body rather than assuming they all matched the "loading flag" shape. 4 have **no synchronous `setState` at all** (every update happens after an `await`) — this rule's static analysis is flagging the async function *call*, not an actual violation, the same false-positive shape reported upstream in facebook/react#34743. Of the other 4, 3 already default their loading state to the value they'd synchronously set anyway (`useState(true)` / `useState('checking')`), so React's own same-value bail-out means no extra render actually happens — the lint rule just can't see that runtime equality. The 4th, `AdminGameManager`, had a real one-render mismatch (defaulted `false`, set `true` synchronously on mount) and got the actual fix: default changed to `true`, so its "..." loading indicator shows from the first render instead of one render late. The warning stays (the synchronous call is still needed for its 5s poll's re-fetches) but the redundant render is gone.

Full per-site reasoning recorded in `eslint.config.js` (line 103's block) so this doesn't need re-deriving next time someone looks at the count.

### Ops
`5eba257` (the `/koniec` docs commit atop this version's code) deployed and verified live 2026-07-31 — bundle-grepped: the served `index-*.js` embeds `"3.1.80"` and that commit hash directly, no ambiguity about the version-label-lags-the-deploy pattern seen in prior sessions. Two dashboard reports flipped resolved on confirmation: `fb:89d83c39` (TV-mode glossary access, fixed v3.1.64) and `fb:2948cf19` (deploy-banner clipboard copy, fixed v3.1.77) — dashboard now **7 open**, all previously tracked.

**Verification:** typecheck clean throughout every step (caught 3 now-unused type imports lint flagged that typecheck alone didn't — `GamePhase`/`Player` in `GameLayout.tsx`/`TVDisplay.tsx`, `Card` in `NegotiationModal.tsx`), lint exit 0 (0 errors / 37 warnings — the 19 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings plus the 18 remaining `set-state-in-effect`, both accounted for), full fast suite 2501 passed / 1 skipped (2502; the +5 is the new `GameLayoutTransitionClear` test file), build clean. Live-verified in a real browser against the built app served through Express: 2-player game creation, taking an action and confirming the dice-result flow + tab-broadcast still work, the glossary panel's term-selection and reset-on-close (both freshly changed) confirmed correct by reopening after close and seeing the browse list rather than a stuck selection — all with zero console errors throughout. `SpaceExplorerPanel` and `TVDisplay` could not be live-verified: the former is reachable only through a narrow playtest-tour deep link that didn't reproduce cleanly in this session, the latter is gated behind TV mode's real "all phones must connect" hard-block (`SpaceExplorerPanel`'s own test file mocks out the entire real component already — a known pre-existing testability gap, not something this session introduced or could fix as a side effect). Both got the same careful render-time-comparison/`useSyncExternalStore` treatment already proven live in six other components, plus a clean typecheck — real but lower-confidence coverage than the rest of this batch, and worth a manual playtest pass on real hardware before fully trusting.

## [3.1.78] - 2026-07-30

### Added: CSP, HSTS, and Permissions-Policy headers — the survey TODO.md asked for, done properly
Deferred 2026-07-25 (see that entry) because a wrong policy could silently break the live site in ways the test suite can't catch — jsdom doesn't enforce CSP at all, and this app leans on inline `style={{...}}` everywhere plus a live cross-origin iframe (the dictionary panel, `dashboard.unravelcodes.com`). Done now with the full survey that was missing, not a quick pass.

**The survey.** Grepped every `fetch`/`WebSocket`/`<iframe>`/image origin across `src/` and `index.html`'s own markup rather than guessing. Findings that shaped the policy: `getBackendURL()` in `networkDetection.ts` resolves same-origin in production, so the ~20 internal API call sites needed no special-casing; three external origins are genuinely reached — `dashboard.unravelcodes.com` (remote config, live glossary fetch, the dictionary iframe), `api.github.com` (the version-sync-status ping), and `iqarius.com` (glossary term images, `src/dictionary/data/glossary.json`'s `imageUrl` fields); `html2canvas`'s feedback-screenshot capture renders to a `data:` URI; the PWA service worker (`public/sw.js`) needs `worker-src`; no `eval`/`Function` constructor anywhere in `src/`, no external fonts, no `<form action>` that submits natively. A second `getBackendURL()` in `deviceDetection.ts` (hardcoded port 3001) turned out to be dead code — nothing imports it, everything imports the same-origin version from `networkDetection.ts` — so it wasn't a connect-src concern, just a stray unused export (left as-is, out of scope here).

**One real fix the survey forced.** `index.html` carried a genuine inline `<script>` (the module-load error handler + the "Reload Page" button, which used an inline `onclick="window.location.reload()"` attribute — CSP governs both the same way). A hash-pinned CSP exemption was the tempting shortcut but a real maintenance trap: any future edit to that script would silently break until someone remembered to recompute the hash. Moved it to [public/error-handler.js](public/error-handler.js) instead — an ordinary same-origin file — and swapped the inline `onclick` for `addEventListener`, since inline event-handler attributes need the same CSP allowance as inline `<script>` blocks. `script-src` is now `'self'` with zero hashes and zero `'unsafe-inline'` to maintain by hand. `style-src` does keep `'unsafe-inline'` — React's `style={{...}}` renders as literal `style="..."` attributes throughout this codebase, which CSP treats the same as a `<style>` tag; there's no realistic way to eliminate that without ripping out inline styles app-wide, and CSS injection is a much smaller attack surface than script injection (UI redress/exfil via crafted selectors, not code execution).

**The policy** (full reasoning inline in [server.js](server.js)'s security-headers block): `default-src 'self'`; `script-src 'self' https://static.cloudflareinsights.com` (that last one is Cloudflare's own auto-injected analytics beacon at the edge — allowed so this change doesn't silently start blocking it as a side effect); `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`; `img-src 'self' data: https://iqarius.com`; `connect-src 'self' https://dashboard.unravelcodes.com https://api.github.com`; `frame-src https://dashboard.unravelcodes.com`; `worker-src 'self'`; `object-src 'none'`; `base-uri 'self'`; `form-action 'self'`; `frame-ancestors 'none'` (the CSP-native form of the `X-Frame-Options: DENY` already set); `upgrade-insecure-requests`. Permissions-Policy restricts only features confirmed unused anywhere in `src/` — camera, microphone, geolocation, payment, usb, and motion sensors — and deliberately leaves `clipboard-write` and `fullscreen` unlisted/default-allowed, since `ShareGameButton`, `PlaytesterLandingPage`, and `ShutdownNotice` (v3.1.77) all call `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`, and `GameLayout`/`ProjectProgress` both call `requestFullscreen()` for TV mode. HSTS is `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` — no `preload`, since that submits to the browser-shipped preload list and is close to irreversible, not something to opt into without an explicit ask.

**Live-browser verification, not just green tests.** Built the app, served it through Express exactly as production does (not the Vite dev server, which never passes through this middleware), and drove it with a real browser: player setup → game creation → full board render (WebSocket connect under `connect-src 'self'`), the feedback button's `html2canvas` screenshot capture (the `data:` URI path), the glossary panel, and the service worker registration — all clean, zero CSP console violations, throughout. Directly injected the exact iframe URL the dictionary panel would use (`https://dashboard.unravelcodes.com/dictionary?termId=...&embedded=true`) and the exact `iqarius.com` image URL as targeted spot-checks: the image loaded successfully confirming `img-src`, and the iframe produced no CSP violation (this sandbox's browser couldn't reach that specific host to fully confirm the load succeeded, but CSP blocks are never silent — they always log a console error — so the absence of one is a reliable negative result). Full suite: 2502 passed / 1 skipped, typecheck clean, lint exit 0 (0 errors / 53 warnings, unchanged), build clean.

## [3.1.77] - 2026-07-30

### Fix: deploy banner's game code is now tap-to-copy
Filed on the dashboard 2026-07-27 (`fb:2948cf19`): "when deploying new code a yellow banner shows up with game code - the code number should be added to clipboard." [ShutdownNotice.tsx](src/components/common/ShutdownNotice.tsx) already rendered the rejoin code inline in the deploy-restart banner; the code is now a tap target that calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` and swaps in "— Copied!" for 2.5s. Deliberately **not** an automatic write on show — `writeText()` needs a secure context and, in some browsers, a user gesture, so an unprompted call can silently fail or throw; the rejection path is swallowed rather than surfaced, since the code stays readable in the banner either way as a fallback. 5 new tests (`tests/components/common/ShutdownNotice.test.tsx`, previously untested) cover copy-success, the 2.5s revert, the rejection path not throwing or corrupting state, and the existing dismiss behavior.
